A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same JADAI research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across additions, relocations, and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original Location Finding, CES, and MNIST Image Discovery experiments, including benchmark scores, implementation ablations, noise tests, and posterior visualizations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds design-prior mix-in ablations and quantitative posterior comparisons with MCMC and ALINE in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The policy, summary, and posterior networks, diffusion/flow-matching losses, stop-gradient operations, training curricula, and inference procedure remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 expands the existing steps; the corrected density-ratio derivation does not change the implemented objective.

E1.justification: Both versions cover one- and two-source Location Finding, CES, and MNIST Image Discovery with the same noise conditions. The added posterior evaluation and exploration ablations reuse the existing two-source Location Finding task.

E2.justification: Appendix B.3 adds MCMC references and an explicitly trained ALINE comparator for two-source posterior evaluation. ALINE already appeared in v1's one-source Location Finding and CES comparisons, but not this posterior comparison. Comparator membership in Tables 1 and 2 remains unchanged.

E3.justification: The new posterior evaluation measures empirical Wasserstein distances to MCMC and ground truth after 30 measurements, using squared Euclidean cost and accounting for mode switching. New exploration ablations compare direct joint training and annealed mix-in against pretraining. The retained benchmark protocols are otherwise stable.

E4.justification: Appendix B.2 newly tests the choice of design-prior mix-in regime. Appendix B.3 adds a diagnostic stress test of multimodal posterior representation using MCMC, ground truth, and ALINE. Existing BPTT, rollout-length, and measurement-noise analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Table 3 retains mean ± SE over five seeds, and the figures retain interquartile bands. New results use the existing mean ± SE convention without reporting a changed run count or a new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 retain their numerical results. New mix-in results are 12.348 ± 0.068 for direct training and 12.352 ± 0.044 for annealing. New Table 4 reports W(JADAI, MCMC) = 0.07 ± 0.01 and W(ALINE, MCMC) = 3.64 ± 0.16. Image Discovery training time changes from approximately 48 to 15.7 hours, without establishing comparable hardware.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.1 substantially expands the formal treatment through per-horizon Barber–Agakov/KL-gap identities and the connection between summed posterior losses and gap gradients for density models, distinguishing score/flow surrogates. Equations 13–14 also correct v1's telescoping identity by restoring the initial posterior-to-prior term and defining the initial density loss.

C1.justification: The central claims remain joint amortization of adaptive design and inference, flexible intermediate posteriors, and competitive benchmark performance. The abstract now explicitly says 'without density evaluations,' but this capability was already explained in v1's Section 3.2.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new posterior results as evidence that diffusion captures exchangeable multimodal structure better than ALINE's GMM, while qualifying the comparison as a stress test rather than a reproduction. It also expands practical guidance connecting exploration regimes to the informativeness of random designs.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access statement, POT implementation details, and rollout-only timings of 0.04 seconds for Location Finding and 0.02 seconds for CES. It removes the Image Discovery GPU specification when revising training time. The new generic curriculum duration below 1% of training time is not reconciled with the retained Image Discovery schedule spanning 5% of training steps.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting diffusion-objective reasoning, optimal-transport computation, and differentiable simulators. The main related-work positioning remains intact. Updates from preprints to published entries, including ALINE, refer to existing works rather than new comparators.

P1.justification: Localized revisions clarify stop-gradients and training choices, expand algorithm wording, subdivide Appendix B, and add an Impact Statement and code-availability section. Front matter and bibliography metadata are updated, while the overall narrative structure remains stable.

P2.justification: v2 adds the posterior-quality Table 4 and expands Algorithm 1's display. Existing figures and tables are retained, with several relocated and later tables renumbered. Captions clarify baseline provenance and missing entries; there is no wholesale visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The corrected telescoping identity, additional posterior checks and exploration ablations, clearer training explanations, and code-access statement strengthen an otherwise stable paper. These gains are limited by sparse MCMC/ALINE evaluation details, a surrogate-loss argument that does not establish its asserted per-step BA-gap reduction, and less clear timing/hardware disclosures. Overall, the revision provides useful additional support and clarity without fully resolving these methodological documentation gaps.
